subject: Seller invoice owner & SLA credit routing for ACME marketplace addendum
messages:
From: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum question — invoicing + SLA credits

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement flagged two items on the draft marketplace addendum we wanted to confirm before we move to legal:

1) Invoice ownership — our billing team expects the seller on the Order Form to be the party that issues invoices to end customers. Will Redwood act as the invoice owner for marketplace-originated orders, or do you expect the reseller (ACME) to be the invoice owner?

2) SLA credits / service refunds — the draft includes a general pass-through line for credits, but procurement needs clarification on whether Redwood will allow SLA credits to flow through the reseller to the end customer (or whether credits will be handled as reductions/credits on Redwood invoices). We need the mechanics spelled out for audit and revenue recognition.

I've attached the current addendum draft — redlines to follow if needed. Short timeline: we want to close commercial terms by next Wednesday. Can you confirm the intended invoice flow and high-level approach to credits?

Attachments: [acme_marketplace_addendum_draft.pdf]

Thanks,
Jordan Fields
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
ACME Cloud

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum question — invoicing + SLA credits

Ben / Karthik — looping you in. Jordan's asks are exactly what procurement will escalate during MSA/Order Form sign-off. Quick notes from my side:

- Prefer Redwood to remain the invoice owner for marketplace orders where Redwood is the billed service provider. This keeps revenue recognition simple and prevents double-invoicing.
- We can provide a pass-through mechanics section but need to limit our exposure on credits/refunds. Specifically: credits that originate from infra/runtime SLA failures should be handled on Redwood's billing for customers we bill directly; for reseller-originated billing we need a contractual assignment (or a holdback) so Redwood is not left with open-ended refund liability.

Ben — can you draft a short redline that: (a) states "Redwood will be the invoice owner unless the Order Form explicitly designates the Reseller as Seller"; (b) introduces a cap and evidence requirement for pass-through credits; and (c) includes an indemnity carve for credits triggered by reseller-approved customizations?

Karthik — ops question for you: if we remain invoice owner but allow conditional pass-through, what operational controls are needed (invoicing metadata, customer mappings, reporting to reseller) and can we support them within a two-week implementation window?

Laura — can you do a quick legal sanity check on the proposed language below when Ben sends a redline?

I'll reply to Jordan once Ben and Karthik confirm.

—Marissa
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum question — invoicing + SLA credits (proposed redline)

Marissa / Karthik / Laura —

Attached is a first-pass redline (stubbed here):

--- PROPOSED ADDENDUM LANGUAGE (excerpt) ---
1. Invoice Owner. Unless the Order Form expressly names the Reseller as the Seller, Redwood Inference, Inc. ("Redwood") shall be the invoice owner and shall issue invoices to End Customers.

2. SLA Credits and Pass-Through. If, and only if, (a) Redwood remains the invoice owner, and (b) the Reseller provides documented evidence of the End Customer's claim and a signed credit assignment in favor of Redwood, Redwood may (at its sole discretion) provide a corresponding credit to the Reseller which the Reseller may elect to pass through to the End Customer. Any Pass-Through Credit shall be limited to the amount of the credit actually issued by Redwood and shall be subject to a cap equal to the sum of Redwood's charges for the affected billing period.

3. Reseller Liability for Credits. The Reseller shall indemnify and hold harmless Redwood from any third-party claims relating to credits that arise from Reseller-configured or Reseller-authorized customizations, provided that Redwood's liability for SLA Credits unrelated to Reseller modifications shall be limited to the amounts Redwood actually receives from its provider invoicing systems.

--- end excerpt ---

Notes / open questions:
- Cap language: propose we limit to the charges for the billing period (keeps it measurable).
- Evidence: require a standard template for credit requests (invoice #, customer ID, incident ID).
- Ops impact: we'll need an internal flag on orders marked "Reseller billed" and a verification flow to accept signed assignments before credits are applied.

Attachments: [rdw_proposed_redline.docx] — the doc contains the full blackline and an appendix with the evidence template.

If this direction looks good I can send this to Jordan with a short Ops/Legal build timeline. Laura — please flag any legal issues (assignment language, indemnity carve).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Partner Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum question — invoicing + SLA credits (position & next steps)

Jordan / ACME procurement — thanks for surfacing this. Quick internal position and operational ask so we can move to signature: 

1) Position (commercial): Redwood is prepared to be the default invoice owner for marketplace-originated Order Forms. If ACME requires to be designated as Seller (invoice owner), we will consider it but require a separate credit assignment and limited liability carve (see below).

2) SLA credits / pass-through mechanics: Redwood will support pass-through of SLA credits to the End Customer only under these conditions: (a) Redwood is the invoice owner or there is an executed credit assignment from the Reseller to Redwood; (b) Reseller submits the standard evidence package (invoice id, incident id, support ticket, and signed customer acknowledgement); (c) the total pass-through for any single claim is capped at Redwood's fees for the affected billing period.

3) Legal / Risk ask: Redwood requires an indemnity from the Reseller for credits that arise out of Reseller-specific changes or reseller-managed provisioning. For native Redwood infra issues, Redwood will retain direct responsibility up to the capped amount.

4) Ops / Implementation: To operationalize this we need: (i) an order attribute "Reseller billed" in our billing system; (ii) a standard credit request template (we've drafted one in the attached redline); and (iii) an acceptance SLA — we propose 10 business days to validate and issue/deny a credit. Ben / Marissa: can you confirm we can meet that 10-business-day SLA for credit validation and whether the evidence template is acceptable?

Next steps: Ben will share the blackline with ACME and Laura will confirm legal language. Once ACME accepts these conditions we'll prepare an Order Form with the Seller field populated and a short ops runbook. HubSpot deal: HS-34219. DocuSign link will be generated after ACME confirms commercial.

Attachments: [rdw_proposed_redline.docx, acme_marketplace_addendum_draft.pdf]

—Karthik Iyer
Head of Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
